map.An equations & inequalities adventure in: A story about equations & inequalities in five chapters. It has six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Pattern distortion detected under city h: Bent patterns found under city hall. Reader: stand by.
map.Previously: a winter blackout turned the: Last time: a winter blackout turned the city grid dark. The crew plotted every district by its coordinates and relit Axiom City. Then the lamps under city hall blinked a message: COME DOWN.
map.Ada Vex built a vault below city hall. T: Ada Vex built a vault below city hall. The blueprints call it the Balance Vault. Tonight, its door is... open.
Open doors are invitations. Or warnings. Nadia, you know the blueprints. Lead.
map.Dungeon level unlocked. Why is the floor: Dungeon level unlocked. Why is the floor... smoking?
That is inequality fog. It seals the exits. Only TRUE statements clear it. False ones feed it.
map.The antechamber. Brass balance scales li: The antechamber. Brass balance scales line the walls. Behind the crew, the fog covers the stairs, and the way back is gone.
map.Every scale in here is an equation — a s: Every scale in here is an equation, a statement that two sides are equal. The pedestal wants a key.
map.So we test keys the way I test bolts. On: So we test keys the way I test bolts. One at a time, no guessing twice.
map.Practice plate: n + 2 = 6. Only n = 4 ke: Practice plate: n + 2 = 6. Only n = 4 keeps it true. 4 + 2 really is 6.
map.Correct. A solution is the value that ma: Correct. A solution is the value that makes the statement TRUE. A wrong key is a lie. The fog likes lies.
map.An equation says two things are equal. A: An equation says two things are equal. A solution is the value that makes it true. Substitute, then check.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. T: Reader, you're our fifth crew member. Test the keys. TRUE statements only.
map.The pedestal plate reads x + 7 = 15. Fou: The pedestal plate reads x + 7 = 15. Four brass keys are stamped 8, 22, 7, 105. Only the key that makes the plate TRUE will turn. Then the fog hisses a second check: does y = 6 make 3y = 21 true?
map.Conceptual: a solution is the value that: Conceptual: a solution is the value that makes an equation TRUE. Substitute the key for x. Then check if both sides really are equal.
map.Procedural: take a key, add 7 to it, and: Procedural: take a key, add 7 to it, and see if you get exactly 15. For the fog's second check, work out 3 × 6 before you answer.
map.The bridge across IS the beam of one gia: The bridge across IS the beam of one giant scale. It only locks level when both pans match.
map.Left pan: a sealed crate — call its weig: Left pan: a sealed crate, with weight x, plus nine brass weights. Right pan: fourteen.
map.Practice beam: n + 3 = 10. Lift 3 off BO: Practice beam: n + 3 = 10. Lift 3 off BOTH pans... n = 7. It never wobbled.
That undo move is an inverse operation. Addition is undone by subtraction, on BOTH sides.
map.Inverse operations undo each other: + an: Inverse operations undo each other: + and −, × and ÷. Balance rule: same move, both sides, every time.
map.Counterweights ready. Reader — level the: Counterweights ready. Reader, level the beam so we can cross!
map.The beam locks only when both pans match: The beam locks only when both pans match. Left pan: the crate x plus 9 brass weights. Right pan: 14 weights. Solve x + 9 = 14. Type x and watch the beam.
map.Conceptual: a scale stays level only if: Conceptual: a scale stays level only if you do the SAME thing to both sides. To get x alone, the 9 next to it must go, from BOTH pans.
map.Procedural: undo + 9 with its inverse: s: Procedural: undo + 9 with its inverse: subtract 9 from both sides. x = 14 − 9. Work it out carefully.
map.Past the bridge: a brass door with two g: Past the bridge: a brass door with two gear locks. Behind the crew, the fog puts out the corridor lamps one by one.
Lock A multiplied x by six and shows 42. Lock B split x into four equal turns and shows one turn: eight.
map.Naming the unknown x tells us exactly wh: Naming the unknown x tells us exactly what each lock DID. Then we undo it. Inverses again.
map.A letter like x stands for the unknown n: A letter like x stands for the unknown number. Say what was done to it. Then use the inverse on both sides.
map.Two locks, two inverses. Spin them, read: Two locks, two inverses. Spin them, reader. The lamps are going out!
map.Two gear locks, one rule each. Lock A: 6: Two gear locks, one rule each. Lock A: 6x = 42. The gear turned x six times over. Lock B: x ÷ 4 = 8. The gear split x into four equal turns. Find each x.
map.Conceptual: name what each lock DID to x: Conceptual: name what each lock DID to x, then undo it with the inverse operation. Multiplication and division undo each other.
map.Procedural: Lock A: 6x means 6 × x, so d: Procedural: Lock A: 6x means 6 × x, so divide 42 by 6. Lock B: x was divided by 4, so multiply 8 by 4.
map.A freight lift waits at the shaft. A bra: A freight lift waits at the shaft. A brass plate states the rule. The fog does not agree.
map.\"At least 12\" isn't one number. Twelve: "At least 12" isn't one number. Twelve works. Thirteen works. Fifty works. How do we even write that?
map.With an inequality — a statement compari: With an inequality, a statement that compares values. It can be true for MANY values at once.
map.Ada's manual graphs one: \"at most 20 de: Ada's manual graphs one: "at most 20 degrees" is t ≤ 20. Draw a FILLED circle on 20 and a ray toward the smaller numbers. Filled means 20 itself counts.
map.Symbols: > greater than · < less than ·: Symbols: > greater than · < less than · ≥ at least (the number is included) · ≤ at most (included).
map.Write the lift's rule, then pick its pic: Write the lift's rule, then pick its picture. The fog reads symbols, reader.
map.The brass plate says the lift runs with: The brass plate says the lift runs with at least 12 crates of ballast. First write the rule as an inequality (x = crates loaded). Then choose its number-line graph.
map.Conceptual: 'at least 12' means exactly: Conceptual: 'at least 12' means exactly 12 is allowed AND anything bigger is allowed. Does the symbol you picked include 12 itself?
map.Procedural: an included boundary gets a: Procedural: an included boundary gets a FILLED (closed) circle. The ray points toward the other values that keep the rule true. For 'at least', those are the bigger numbers.
map.Value cards. Every card that makes the r: Value cards. Every card that makes the rule TRUE opens a vent. Every false one... feeds the fog.
map.All the true values together form the so: All the true values together make the solution set. Strictly less than. The boundary is not invited.
map.Like loot filters. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5: Like loot filters. t < 4 keeps 2 and 3.5, but not 4, because 4 < 4 is false.
map.A solution set is every value that makes: A solution set is every value that makes a statement true. An inequality can have many solutions.
map.Tap every TRUE card, reader. Miss one an: Tap every TRUE card, reader. Miss one and we keep breathing fog.
map.Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EVERY card whose v: Vent rule: v < 9. Tap EVERY card whose value makes the rule true. Those vents open. Tap a false one and the fog gets thicker.
map.Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT — a value jo: Conceptual: v < 9 is STRICT. A value joins the solution set only if it is really smaller than 9. The boundary fails its own rule: 9 < 9 is false.
map.Procedural: test the cards one at a time: Procedural: test the cards one at a time, decimals too. Practice with t < 4: 2 vents because 2 < 4 is true. 4.2 stays sealed because 4.2 < 4 is false.
map.The last chamber. Ada Vex's vault door —: The last chamber. Ada Vex's vault door: three locks, one pressure gauge, fog up to the knees.
map.Balance is not stillness. It is truth, h: Balance is not stillness. It is truth, held steady. Prove three truths and breathe easy.
map.Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lo: Locks 1 and 2 are one-step equations. Lock 3 is the gauge. The door stays open only while p ≤ 15 stays true.
map.Reader — you've leveled beams and read s: Reader, you've leveled beams and read symbols all night. Call the truths!
map.Boss Gate: inverse operations on both si: Boss Gate: inverse operations on both sides, then test the pressure set. Remember what ≤ includes.
map.Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Loc: Ada's vault door. Lock 1: m − 6 = 9. Lock 2: 4t = 36. Lock 3: the door stays open only while the pressure keeps p ≤ 15 true. Choose the reading set that never breaks the rule.
map.Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to i: Conceptual: each lock did ONE thing to its variable. Undo it with the inverse, on BOTH sides. And ≤ means 'less than OR EQUAL': the boundary itself keeps the rule true.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6: Procedural: Lock 1: undo − 6 by ADDING 6 to both sides. Lock 2: undo × 4 by DIVIDING both sides by 4. Lock 3: test EVERY number in a set against the gauge. One false reading seals the door again.
map.The fog's venting — every grate at once!: The fog is venting out of every grate at once! TRUE statements, five for five!
map.And inside: Ada's eighth journal… plus t: And inside: Ada's eighth journal... plus the city ledger she balanced by hand.
map.Achievement: VAULT BREAKER. Sunrise in t: Achievement: VAULT BREAKER. Sunrise in twenty minutes. Pancakes in thirty.
map.New distortion. The harvest dome is glow: A new bent pattern. The harvest dome is glowing wrong at night. Something in there depends on something else... To be continued.
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew captain. Keeps the notebook and asks the next question. This volume: modeled the practice beam and read the lift's rule out loud.
Evidence officer, and tonight's leader. This volume: called every scale an equation and asked for TRUE statements only.
map.Builder and mixer. This volume: built th: Builder and mixer. This volume: built the counterweights that let the crew level the Great Scale.
map.Pattern hunter. This volume: decoded the: Pattern hunter. This volume: figured out the gear locks and filtered the fog cards like loot.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Senses bent patterns but cannot compute. That's your job.
map.Inverse operation.The undo-move: + undon: Inverse operation.The undo move: + is undone by −, × is undone by ÷. Always use it on BOTH sides. x + 9 = 14 → x = 5; 6x = 42 → x = 7; x ÷ 4 = 8 → x = 32.
map.Inequality.A comparison that can be true: Inequality.A comparison that can be true for many values: "at least 12" is x ≥ 12. Closed circle at 12, ray toward the bigger numbers.
map.Solution set.All the values that make it: Solution set.All the values that make it true. For v < 9 that includes 3, 5.5, and 8.9, but never 9 itself.
map.completed Volume 8: The Balance Vault an: completed Volume 8: The Balance Vault and showed skill with equations and solutions, one-step equations, writing and graphing inequalities, and solution sets.
map.Substitute: 6 + 9 = 15 is TRUE — so k =: Substitute: 6 + 9 = 15 is TRUE, so k = 6 IS a solution.
map.Now test k = 3 in 4k = 24: 4 × 3 = 12, n: Now test k = 3 in 4k = 24: 4 × 3 = 12, not 24. So k = 3 is NOT a solution.
map.b = 7. Check by substituting: 7 + 4 = 11: b = 7. Check by substituting: 7 + 4 = 11 ✓. The beam stays level.
map.A thermostat rule says: keep the room at: A thermostat rule says: keep the room at MOST 20 degrees.
map.Graph: a FILLED circle at 20 (20 counts): Graph: a FILLED circle at 20 (20 counts), with the ray pointing LEFT toward the smaller numbers.
map.Solution set: {2, 5.9}. A strict < never: Solution set: {2, 5.9}. A strict < never includes its own boundary.
map.Gauge: the set {18, 20} works — 18 ≤ 20: Gauge: the set {18, 20} works. 18 ≤ 20 is true AND 20 ≤ 20 is true. The boundary counts for ≤.
map.Pick a key first — substitute it for x i: Pick a key first. Substitute it for x in your head.
map.22 won't turn: that's 15 + 7. You combin: 22 won't turn: that's 15 + 7. You put the numbers together. Ask what adds WITH 7 to make 15.
map.7 is already on the plate. Substituting: 7 is already on the plate. Substituting x = 7 gives 7 + 7 = 14. False. The fog thickens.
105 is 15 × 7. Multiplication snuck in. This plate ADDS. Try substituting again.
map.The key fits! Now answer the fog's secon: The key fits! Now answer the fog's second check: yes or no?
map.Careful — substitute it: 3 × 6 makes 18,: Careful: substitute it. 3 × 6 makes 18, not 21. Is that a true statement?
map.x = 8 turns the key (8 + 7 = 15 ✓), and: x = 8 turns the key (8 + 7 = 15 ✓), and you told the fog the truth: 3 × 6 = 18 ≠ 21. A side door opens with a sigh.
map.x = 5. You removed 9 from BOTH sides and: x = 5. You took 9 off BOTH sides and the beam locked level: 5 + 9 = 14. Cross!
map.14 is the whole right pan. First remove: 14 is the whole right pan. First take 9 off BOTH sides. What is left on the right?
map.You ADDED 9. The crate already has 9 bes: You ADDED 9. The crate already has 9 beside it. Undo + 9 by taking 9 off BOTH sides.
map.The beam tips. Remove 9 from BOTH sides: The beam tips. Take 9 off BOTH sides so x stands alone. Then weigh what is left.
map.x = 7 (6 × 7 = 42 ✓) and x = 32 (32 ÷ 4: x = 7 (6 × 7 = 42 ✓) and x = 32 (32 ÷ 4 = 8 ✓). Both gears spin. The door grinds open!
map.36 is 42 − 6. But 6x means 6 TIMES x — s: 36 is 42 − 6. But 6x means 6 TIMES x. Subtraction won't undo a gear. Use the inverse: DIVIDE both sides by 6.
map.2 is 8 ÷ 4 — but x was ALREADY divided b: 2 is 8 ÷ 4. But x was ALREADY divided by 4. Undo division with its inverse: MULTIPLY both sides by 4.
map.A lock still holds. Name the operation d: A lock still holds. Name the operation done to x. Then use its inverse on BOTH sides.
map.Choose the inequality first — read the p: Choose the inequality first. Read the plate again.
map.x > 12 leaves 12 itself OUT — but the pl: x > 12 leaves 12 itself OUT. But the plate says exactly 12 crates is enough to run.
map.x ≤ 12 points the wrong way: 'at least': x ≤ 12 points the wrong way: 'at least' allows MORE ballast, not less.
map.x = 12 allows only exactly 12 — but 13 c: x = 12 allows only exactly 12. But 13 crates or 50 crates also work for 'at least 12.'
map.The symbol is right! Now pick the graph: The symbol is right! Now pick the graph that shows the same truth.
map.An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT included: An OPEN circle means 12 is NOT included. But the lift runs with exactly 12. Look for a filled boundary.
map.That ray slides toward values SMALLER th: That ray goes toward values SMALLER than 12. The lift needs 12 or MORE.
map.A single point shows only x = 12. The ru: A single point shows only x = 12. The rule is true for many values. Where is the ray?
map.x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the: x ≥ 12: closed circle at 12, ray to the right. The lift hums awake and lowers the crew deeper.
map.Tap the cards that make v < 9 TRUE — tes: Tap the cards that make v < 9 TRUE. Test each one.
map.9 < 9 is false — the boundary stays seal: 9 < 9 is false. The boundary stays sealed. A strict < never lets its own boundary through.
map.12 < 9 is false — that card feeds the fo: 12 < 9 is false. That card feeds the fog. Only values SMALLER than 9 clear it.
map.Solution set {3, 5.5, 8.9} — three true: Solution set {3, 5.5, 8.9}: three true statements, three vents wide open. The gallery clears!
map.True values are still fogged in. EVERY c: True values are still stuck in the fog. EVERY card smaller than 9 is in the solution set, decimals too.
map.Lock 1 holds. 9 − 6 undoes the WRONG way: Lock 1 holds. 9 − 6 undoes it the WRONG way. 6 was taken AWAY from m, so give 6 back: add 6 to both sides.
map.Lock 1 holds. Undo − 6 with its inverse:: Lock 1 holds. Undo − 6 with its inverse: add 6 to BOTH sides.
map.Lock 2 holds. You multiplied — but 4t me: Lock 2 holds. You multiplied. But 4t already means 4 × t. Undo × 4 by dividing both sides by 4.
map.Lock 2 holds. 4t means 4 × t. Apply the: Lock 2 holds. 4t means 4 × t. Use the inverse of multiplication on both sides.
map.Two locks open! Now choose the pressure: Two locks open! Now choose the pressure set for Lock 3.
map.Lock 3 holds. 15 ≤ 15 is true… but 16 ≤: Lock 3 holds. 15 ≤ 15 is true... but 16 ≤ 15 is FALSE. One bad reading seals the door again.
map.Lock 3 holds. 16 ≤ 15 is false and 20 ≤: Lock 3 holds. 16 ≤ 15 is false and 20 ≤ 15 is false. That set slams the door twice.
map.Lock 3 holds. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 1: Lock 3 holds. 0 ≤ 15 is true, but 22 ≤ 15 is false. EVERY reading must keep the rule true.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9, and {12,: ALL LOCKS OPEN. m = 15, t = 9, and {12, 15} keeps p ≤ 15 true. 15 ≤ 15 counts! The fog vents skyward. The Balance Vault yields.
